q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Today is August 22, 2026. **4 days remain** until the earnings announcement and forward guidance release.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which will be announced on August 26. This is asking what guidance NVIDIA will provide for Q3 FY2027 (the next quarter) when they announce Q2 FY2027 results.

The research provides NVIDIA's **current guidance for Q2 FY2027** (issued May 20, 2026): $91.0 billion ±2%, or $89.2–92.8 billion range. However, the question is asking for the **forward guidance** they will issue on August 26 for the quarter after Q2.

Key observations:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion (exceeded guidance by ~$2 billion)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance (current): $91.0 billion ±2%
- Wall Street consensus for Q2: $91.9 billion
- Year-over-year growth: Q2 vs. year-ago quarter grew from $46.7B to ~$91B (nearly 95% growth)

For forward guidance on Q3 FY2027:
- Historical pattern: NVIDIA has been conservative with guidance and beating it (Q1 beat by ~$2B)
- Sequential growth: Q1 to Q2 shows ~12% sequential growth ($81.6B to $91.0B guidance)
- Industry context: AI/data center demand remains robust, but growth rates typically decelerate sequentially as capacity constraints ease
- If Q2 comes in near the high end (~$92.8B) and sequential growth moderates to 8-10%, Q3 guidance would likely be in the $100-103 billion range

However, given:
- Conservative guidance practices
- Potential geopolitical constraints (China restrictions mentioned)
- Market maturation reducing explosive growth rates
- The range provided ($99.5–115.5B) suggests the forecaster expects guidance somewhat above current levels

**Most likely outcome: $100-107 billion** for Q3 FY2027 forward guidance, representing modest sequential growth from Q2 guided levels.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Weaker-than-expected Q2 actual results (below $91.0B guidance)
- Deteriorating demand signals from major customers (hyperscalers pulling back orders)
- Increased geopolitical tensions or additional China restrictions
- Supply chain disruptions or yield issues
- Conservative pre-guidance to manage expectations further
- Market saturation in near term after strong recent quarters
- Macro economic weakness affecting enterprise spending

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Q2 actual results significantly exceed guidance (like the $2B beat in Q1)
- Accelerating AI adoption driving stronger customer orders
- New product launches or architectural advantages gaining traction
- Easing of China restrictions or new markets opening
- Data center capex budgets higher than anticipated
- Cloud providers accelerating GPU procurement cycles
- Margin expansion allowing higher revenue targets at same profitability
- Continued sequential acceleration defying typical deceleration patterns

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**From the research provided:**
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6 billion
- Q1 FY2027 guidance was beaten by ~$2 billion
- Q2 FY2027 current guidance: $91.0 billion ±2% ($89.2–92.8B range)
- Sequential growth Q1→Q2 guidance: ~12%
- Year-over-year growth: ~95% (from $46.7B to ~$91B)

Historical pattern from research: NVIDIA has beaten guidance in recent quarters. However, forward guidance typically becomes more conservative as quarters progress and demand patterns solidify.

For Q3 FY2027 guidance (to be issued in 4 days), assuming:
- Q2 actual lands near $91–92B (upper end of guidance)
- Sequential growth moderates from 12% to 8–10% range
- Conservative cushion for guidance

**Estimated forward guidance range: $100.0–107.0 billion**

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, after the close of trading [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, calls for revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion, which falls within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This represents a significant increase from the year-ago quarter's revenue of $46.7 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
